flight-plan.context: A clipboard form with a small airplane on top and a route joining two dots. Used for flight planning tools, route filing, dispatch screens and trip itineraries.

notam.context: A sheet of paper with a warning triangle and a small airplane above lines of text. Used for notices to pilots, airspace alerts, airport closures and aviation bulletins.

metar-report.context: A paper strip with a wind barb at the left and lines of coded text. Used for aviation weather reports, airport observations and pilot weather briefings.

go-around.context: An airplane climbing away along a curved path just above a runway line. Used for missed approach, aborted landing and approach procedure screens.

touch-and-go.context: A dashed flight path dipping down to a runway line and rising again, with an airplane at the end. Used for pattern practice, landing drills and flight training logs.

flight-level.context: An airplane in side view flying along a level beside a vertical altitude scale with ticks. Used for cruising altitude, air traffic clearances and altitude displays.

ditching.context: An airplane in side view floating on water with wavy lines around its body. Used for water landing procedures, sea safety and emergency training.

red-eye-flight.context: An airplane flying past a crescent moon with a few small stars. Used for overnight flights, late departures and night travel filters in booking tools.

frequent-flyer.context: A membership card with a small airplane, text lines and a row of three stars. Used for airline loyalty programs, miles balances and status tiers.

seat-upgrade.context: An airline seat in side view next to a thick upward arrow. Used for cabin class upgrades, premium seat offers and booking add-ons.

fragile-baggage-tag.context: A luggage tag on a looped strap printed with a wine glass. Used for fragile item handling, special baggage labels and airline check-in options.

heavy-baggage-tag.context: A luggage tag on a looped strap printed with a kettlebell weight. Used for overweight bag warnings, heavy item labels and baggage allowance screens.

restricted-airspace.context: A map area with a closed irregular outline and short hatch ticks along its inside edge. Used for controlled zones, military areas and airspace maps.

no-fly-zone.context: A dashed circular boundary with a bar across its centre and a small airplane outside it. Used for drone bans, flight exclusion areas and geofencing alerts.

flight-strip.context: A long narrow paper strip divided into columns with short text marks. Used for air traffic control tools, callsign lists and tower workflow screens.

remove-before-flight-tag.context: A long streamer tag with a swallow tail, a hole at the top and bold lettering lines. Used for pre-flight checks, maintenance reminders and ground crew safety items.

air-traffic-control-console.context: A desk console with two radar screens standing above it. Used for air traffic control, airport tower and radar monitoring content.

airspace-classes.context: Stepped layers of airspace, widest at the top, above a small airport tower and ground line. Used for airspace diagrams, controlled zone charts and pilot training.

crosswind-landing.context: An airplane angled toward a runway with wind arrows pointing in from one side. Used for crosswind limits, landing conditions and weather warnings.

emergency-landing.context: An airplane descending toward a runway line with a flame beside it. Used for engine failure, forced landing and aviation incident content.

mayday.context: A large exclamation mark between curved radio wave arcs on both sides. Used for distress calls, urgent radio alerts and emergency communication.

flight-diverted.context: A dashed route that forks, with one branch crossed out and the other ending at a dot. Used for diversion notices, rerouted flights and alternate airport alerts.

regional-jet.context: A slim airliner in side view with a high T-shaped tail and engines on the rear fuselage. Used for short haul airline fleets and regional route listings.

trijet.context: An airliner in side view with an engine under the wing and a third engine at the base of the tail fin. Used for aircraft type lists and aviation history pages.

bush-plane.context: A high-wing single propeller plane in side view with wing struts and fat tundra tires. Used for backcountry flying, remote travel and adventure content.

warbird.context: A vintage single-seat propeller fighter seen from above with oval wings and a bubble canopy. Used for air shows, aviation museums and history content.

twin-boom-aircraft.context: An aircraft from above with a central pod and wing, two long tail booms and a tail joining them. Used for aircraft type lists and unusual airframe guides.

flight-booking.context: A calendar page with a small airplane in one date and a check mark beside it. Used for flight reservation, travel date selection and booking confirmation.

four-forces-of-flight.context: A small airplane seen from above with four arrows pointing up, down, forward and backward. Used for physics lessons, flight training and aerodynamics diagrams.

afterburner.context: A flared jet exhaust nozzle in side view with a long flame behind it. Used for fighter jets, engine thrust and supersonic flight content.

boarding-pass-reader.context: A slanted pedestal scanner with a boarding pass held above its glass window. Used for gate scanning, self boarding and ticket validation.

gate-podium.context: A counter desk with a screen on top and a number sign on a post beside it. Used for boarding gates, gate agent desks and departure information.

in-flight-map.context: A seatback screen showing a dashed arc between two dots with a small airplane along it. Used for flight trackers, entertainment systems and journey progress.

aircraft-lightning-strike.context: An airplane in flight with a jagged lightning bolt touching its wing. Used for thunderstorm hazards, weather incidents and aircraft safety content.

formation-flight.context: Three small jets in a V formation, each trailing a straight line. Used for air shows, display teams and military flypast content.

plane-spotting.context: A person holding binoculars up to look at a small airplane overhead. Used for aviation hobby, airport viewing areas and enthusiast communities.

baggage-handler.context: A ground crew worker with ear defenders lifting a suitcase with both hands. Used for ramp services, luggage loading and airport staff roles.

pilot-logbook.context: An open hardcover book with ruled lines on the left page and a small airplane on the right. Used for recording flight hours, training progress and pilot records.

pilot-license.context: An identification card with a small portrait square and an airplane silhouette. Used for pilot certificates, aviator credentials and flight school records.

closed-runway-marking.context: A runway strip seen from above with a large X painted across it. Used for runway closures, airport hazard markings and ground safety notices.

passenger-manifest.context: A clipboard with a small airplane at the top and rows of people listed below it. Used for passenger lists, crew rosters and boarding counts.

baggage-claim-ticket.context: A small slip with barcode bars and a tear-off stub divided by a perforated line. Used for luggage receipts, lost baggage claims and check-in paperwork.

damaged-baggage.context: A hard shell suitcase with a zigzag crack across its face and a detached wheel. Used for baggage damage claims, airline complaints and luggage insurance.

balloon-burner.context: A hot air balloon burner on a frame above a basket rim, with a tall flame rising from it. Used for ballooning, inflation and flame heat content.

aisle-wheelchair.context: A narrow upright transfer chair with a tall back, push handle and small wheels. Used for assisted boarding, accessibility services and reduced mobility support.

fuel-dumping.context: An airliner from above with two dashed spray trails streaming from behind its wing tips. Used for fuel jettison, emergency landing preparation and incident reports.

barrel-roll.context: A small airplane trailing a looping corkscrew line behind it. Used for aerobatics, stunt flying and air show content.

aviation-obstruction-light.context: A tall thin mast with a round lamp on top and short glow rays around it. Used for tower beacons, chimney warning lights and low flying hazard marking.

runway-end-identifier-lights.context: A runway end seen from above with a flashing light and arc on each side of it. Used for runway threshold lighting and airport approach guidance.

weight-and-balance.context: A small airplane and a weight block resting on opposite ends of a plank balanced on a triangle. Used for load sheets, centre of gravity checks and aircraft loading.

overhead-panel.context: A ceiling panel seen from below filled with rows of small toggle switches. Used for cockpit systems, flight deck controls and aircraft simulators.

flight-simulator.context: An enclosed cockpit capsule with a windshield, mounted on four angled hydraulic legs. Used for pilot training, motion platforms and aviation education.
